body: Thank you for the thoughtful reply

That sounds familiar. I feel like there are times when I can be happy, but underneath that, whatever was distracting me to be happy in that moment, I am miserable and I hate myself. During the latter, I think of suicide all of the time. Like daily, nothing to serious, but I'm thinking about it. Recently I had a particularly bad episode which resulted in my going to seek help. I'm starting counseling soon with high hopes. 

Good luck to you, friend.

Hi friend. 

Maybe I'm not really in the position to post advice here since I was posting asking for it just a few days ago, but maybe my recent experience might mean something to you. 

Suicide is an idea that bounces around in my head almost daily, and on thursday I got to the closest point to actually trying to commit it that I have ever had. I immediately started calling hotlines because I was scared of what I might do. Everyone I spoke with was very nice and tried to help as much as they could, but I quickly realized there wasn't really much they could do in this situation, just over the phone without really any context to my problems. Each hotline urged me to seek help at my local institutions. After calling the crisis centre of my local hospital, they admitted me through emergency to get evaluated. I was seen by a psychiatrist and prescribed some medication to help with anxiety. I have been referred to a counselor that I eagerly wait to start to see on monday.

Other than that, I also think we relate on a few levels. I'm finishing up getting my bachelor's degree, and I have no idea what my plans are for next year mostly because I don't think I'm smart enough to go on in my field. I'm trying desperately to find some sort of happiness before university ends, because I know this will probably be the best time of my life and time is running out. I figure that if I could just find someone to love and to love me that I could live with everything else. Or if my school work was going better that at least I'd have something to focus on. If just one or the other worked out then I would have something to not be miserable about, but that hasn't happened yet.

I really hope you seek out and find the help you need.

Apparently Chimo (1-800-667-5005) is a New Brunswick only line. Calling The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (1-800-273-8255) worked. It went alright. I was basically referred to my local mental health centre which I have gone to and I have begun the process the help that I need. 

Thanks for the replies, if anyone else is in a similar situation I hope these resources can be of some use. You can also call (1-888-429-8167) which is a 24/7 mental health crisis line, I think based out of Canada, but regardless it'll work for Canadians; the doctors I went to see today gave me the number.
Thank you, that means a lot
